title: Dexmedetomidine activates the PKA/CREB pathway and inhibits proinflammatory factor expression through beta2 adrenergic receptors.
one_liner_zh: 该文研究右美托咪定通过β2肾上腺素受体激活PKA/CREB通路抑制炎症因子表达，虽涉及分子对接但核心是细胞信号通路与炎症调控，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Dexmedetomidine (DEX) is primarily utilized for sedation in the context of general anesthesia or intensive care. However, the exact regulatory mechanism by which DEX affects cytokines remains unclear. This study aims to investigate the underlying mechanism by which DEX inhibits proinflammatory factors through activation of the beta2 adrenergic receptor (beta2 AR). METHODS: The inflammatory cell model of human mononuclear macrophage (THP-1) cells induced by lipopolysaccharide (LPS) was established to study the effect of DEX on the expression of cell-related inflammatory factors. ADRA2A gene knockout THP-1 cells (THP-1(KO) ) were constructed by CRISPR technology, and the effect of DEX on the expression of inflammatory factors of THP-1(KO) cells was detected. The target sites of DEX on beta2 AR were screened by molecular docking. Reversion experiments were performed using ADRB2-siRNA. Western blot was used to detect the activation of beta2 AR/PKA/CREB pathway and NF-kappaB, and ELISA was used to detect the release level of inflammatory factors. RESULTS: The results demonstrated a significant reduction in the expression levels of MCP-1, interleukin-06, and IL-8 in both THP-1 and THP-1(KO) cells when induced by LPS following treatment with DEX. Additionally, DEX treatment led to an increase in IL-10 expression. Immunofluorescence analysis revealed an upregulation of beta2 AR expression after DEX treatment. Western blot results indicated that DEX notably enhanced the activation of the beta2 AR and PKA/CREB pathways, while concurrently suppressing the activation of NF-kappaB. Notably, the use of ADRB2 siRNA reversed the effects of DEX treatment and promoted the release of inflammatory cytokines. CONCLUSION: DEX initiates the activation of the PKA/CREB pathway through the activation of beta2 AR. Simultaneously, it exerts an inhibitory effect on the activation of NF-kappaB, consequently reducing the transcription of proinflammatory factors while increasing the transcription of anti-inflammatory factors.
abstract_zh: 引言：右美托咪定（DEX）主要用于全身麻醉或重症监护中的镇静。然而，DEX影响细胞因子的确切调控机制尚不清楚。本研究旨在探讨DEX通过激活β2肾上腺素能受体（beta2 AR）抑制促炎因子的潜在机制。方法：建立脂多糖（LPS）诱导的人单核巨噬细胞（THP-1）炎症细胞模型，研究DEX对细胞相关炎症因子表达的影响。通过CRISPR技术构建ADRA2A基因敲除的THP-1细胞（THP-1(KO)），并检测DEX对THP-1(KO)细胞炎症因子表达的影响。通过分子对接筛选DEX在beta2 AR上的靶点。使用ADRB2-siRNA进行回复实验。采用Western blot检测beta2 AR/PKA/CREB通路及NF-kappaB的激活情况，ELISA检测炎症因子的释放水平。结果：结果表明，在LPS诱导后，DEX处理显著降低了THP-1和THP-1(KO)细胞中MCP-1、白细胞介素-06和IL-8的表达水平。此外，DEX处理导致IL-10表达增加。免疫荧光分析显示，DEX处理后beta2 AR表达上调。Western blot结果表明，DEX显著增强了beta2 AR和PKA/CREB通路的激活，同时抑制了NF-kappaB的激活。值得注意的是，使用ADRB2 siRNA逆转了DEX处理的效果，并促进了炎症细胞因子的释放。结论：DEX通过激活beta2 AR启动PKA/CREB通路的激活。同时，它对NF-kappaB的激活发挥抑制作用，从而减少促炎因子的转录，同时增加抗炎因子的转录。
